title: Integrating Telehealth to Advance Lung Cancer Screening
official: Integrating Telehealth to Advance Lung Cancer Screening
summary:
The goal of this pragmatic trial is to learn if telehealth strategies can increase shared decision-making (SDM) for lung cancer screening (LCS). It will also learn about the equity of these strategies by conducting non-inferiority analysis by race and sex. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does patient outreach using synchronous and asynchronous telehealth strategies increase completion of SDM for LCS?
2. Is the effectiveness of these telehealth strategies similar by race and sex?

The study uses a Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trial (SMART) design and includes two stages of interventions. The first stage of intervention includes direct patient outreach with an invitation to schedule either a 1) telehealth SDM visit or 2) telehealth or in-person SDM visit. Participants that do not respond to the first stage interventions receive a text message reminder encouraging SDM completion with or without digital care coordination.
criteria:
Patients who meet the following inclusion criteria will be eligible for the study (assessed at the time of randomization):

1. Age 50 to 77
2. History of tobacco use indicated by either 1) documented 20 pack-year or greater smoking history in their electronic health record (EHR); or 2) self-report via structured survey
3. Currently smokes or formerly smoked cigarettes within the last 15 years
4. Completed a primary care visit at Penn Medicine within 3 years of enrollment
5. Assigned a Penn Medicine primary care provider
6. Documented health insurance of any kind

Patients will be excluded if they do not meet the above criteria or they:

1. Have opted out of research at Penn Medicine
2. Have completed a non-screening chest CT within the past 12 months or screening chest CT in the past 24 months.
3. Have documented history of lung cancer
4. Have documented refusal to complete lung cancer screening
5. Are actively undergoing cancer treatment (excluding low-grade prostate or non-melanoma skin cancer)
6. Have a documented medical condition that may make it inappropriate for them to receive or engage with outreach materials (e.g., treatment-resistant schizophrenia, severe cognitive decline).
